methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly target distributed capability-building outside traditional tech hubs, creating peer-to-peer knowledge transfer that could spread deep fluency beyond metro concentration points.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Commentary explicitly identifying how AI data center concentration in NoVA exacerbates urban-rural divide signals scenario drift toward geographic inequality in both infrastructure access and economic benefit distribution.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI adoption pressure on Richmond's workforce suggests metro-area capability deepening as employment markets demand skills, but concentration in the state capital rather than distributed rural workforce development.

signals.title: How Roanoke College’s new pathways tackle the workforce mismatch - University Business
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's partnership with ed2go for on-demand workforce training platforms signals shallow, platform-mediated skill delivery that achieves geographic distribution but lacks the depth of hands-on AI fluency development.

signals.title: U.Va. pilots three new artificial intelligence literacy courses - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: UVA piloting three AI literacy courses represents institutional commitment to foundational capability-building that could distribute deep fluency if extended beyond flagship university access, though current reach remains concentrated in higher-ed populations.
